tools.name: list_projects
tools.description: List the Fulcrum projects in this organization, with their ids and clients. Call this when you do not already know which project the work in this repository belongs to — every other project-scoped tool accepts either the id or the name this returns.

tools.name: find_features
tools.description: Search the execution board for cards. Every filter is optional and they combine; free text searches card names, task titles, descriptions, product requirements and comments. Returns one summary line per card — call get_feature for the full brief on whichever one you mean to work on. Use it to find work, to see what is already in flight, and to check whether something like this has been built before.

project.description: Project id or an unambiguous part of its name. Omit to search the whole organization.

limit.description: Maximum cards to return (default 50, capped at 200)

tools.name: get_feature
tools.description: Read everything one card asks for: its description, product requirements, estimates by role, task checklist, dependencies in both directions, labels, release, linked branches, approval state and recent comments. Accepts a short id like FUL-17 or a numeric id. This is the tool to call before starting work on a card, and again when you are unsure what it was actually asking for.

feature.description: Short id such as FUL-17, or the numeric card id

tools.name: get_feature_prd
tools.description: Read one card's product requirements in full. get_feature already includes them when they are short, and says so when it has truncated them — call this when it did, or when you need to quote the requirements exactly rather than work from a summary.

feature.description: Short id such as FUL-17, or the numeric card id

tools.name: get_project_prompt
tools.description: Read the estimation context Fulcrum itself uses for a project: the organization's rubric, its delivery roles, the complexity scale, its releases, and the inventory of features this team has already priced. Read it before sizing anything, so the estimate reflects how this team actually sizes work rather than a generic guess. scope 'estimating' is the bundle a local estimate should follow; 'full' also includes the connected repository facts and the closing guidance. Weekly rates are never included in either — this returns hours, never cost.

project.description: Project id or an unambiguous part of its name

tools.name: update_feature
tools.description: Move a card and change its properties: execution status, MoSCoW priority, release, labels and assignees. Use it to keep the board honest while you work — move a card to building when you start and to in_review when you open a pull request, so the team can see where things stand without asking. Every field is optional; only what you name changes, and every change is recorded against your agent identity.

feature.description: Short id such as FUL-17, or the numeric card id

status.description: Execution board column to move the card to

release.description: Exact name of an existing release

tools.name: comment
tools.description: Post a comment on a card, as your own agent identity. This is how you keep the team informed without interrupting anyone: say what you changed and why, record a decision you had to make, or ask a question you cannot answer from the code. Markdown is rendered, and @-mentioning a teammate by their handle actually notifies them — use that when you need a human to decide something.

feature.description: Short id such as FUL-17, or the numeric card id

reply_to.description: Comment id to reply to; omit to start a new thread

tools.name: update_tasks
tools.description: Add items to a card's checklist, or tick them off as you finish them. Ticking items off as you go is what lets somebody watching the board see progress inside a card rather than only when it moves column. Tasks are named by their exact title or their id — get_feature lists both.

feature.description: Short id such as FUL-17, or the numeric card id

complete.description: Task titles or ids to tick off

tools.name: link_branch
tools.description: Attach the git branch, and optionally the pull request, you are building a card on. Do this once you have created the branch: it is what connects the card a reviewer is reading to the code they need to look at. Calling it again for the same branch updates that link rather than adding a second one.

feature.description: Short id such as FUL-17, or the numeric card id

tools.name: propose_prd_change
tools.description: Propose an addition to a card's product requirements. It lands as a PENDING suggestion for a human to accept or reject in Fulcrum — it never edits the requirements directly, so proposing is always safe. Use it when building the card taught you something the requirements do not say: an edge case nobody wrote down, a constraint the code imposes, a decision you had to make. Write the addition itself in markdown, not a description of it.

feature.description: Short id such as FUL-17, or the numeric card id

content.description: The requirement text to add, in markdown

note.description: One line telling the reviewer why; shown in the queue

tools.name: get_prd_suggestions
tools.description: List the pending and recently resolved requirement suggestions on a card, so you can see whether something you proposed was accepted, and avoid proposing the same thing twice.

feature.description: Short id such as FUL-17, or the numeric card id

tools.name: start_work
tools.description: Tell Fulcrum you are starting work on a card. Call it once, before you begin. It opens a numbered work episode so the team can see the card is in hand, and so the time and tokens you spend get attributed to the right work. The role defaults to whichever role carries most of the card's estimate; name one explicitly if you are doing a different kind of work. This does NOT move the card — use update_feature for that, so the board never claims something you did not do.

feature.description: Short id such as FUL-17, or the numeric card id

role.description: Role name or id; defaults to the card's dominant estimated role

session_ref.description: Your harness session id, if you know it

tools.name: finish_work
tools.description: Tell Fulcrum you have stopped working on a card, closing the episode start_work opened. Call it when you finish or when you are handing back to a person — the gap between finishing and the card actually being done is one of the more useful things this measures, and it only exists if you close the episode honestly.

feature.description: Short id such as FUL-17, or the numeric card id

note.description: One line on where you left it
